_about: Hand labels: which assignments truly assess each learning outcome. The pipeline never reads this file; it's only used to score the pipeline. Labels stay fixed while scoring. Change one only if the labeling rule says it's wrong, never to make a score look better.
labeling_rule: Aligned means the assignment explicitly requires students to demonstrate the outcome's skill, named in its title, description, or rubric, even if it isn't the main focus. Coverage that's only implied ('a full-stack app probably has a UI', 'the final covers all midterm topics') doesn't count.
_quote_note: Each outcome is identified by a quote: the syllabus words that state it. For a list item, that's the item itself. Pipeline outcomes are matched to labels by where their own quotes land in the syllabus, so a reworded outcome still meets its label.

CS3200.quote: The primary goal is to make you fluent in relational database design. You should be able to look at a business problem and produce a normalized schema that handles edge cases.
CS3200.note: FINAL covers 'all midterm topics' but never names design or normalization, so under the labeling rule it doesn't count.

CS3200.quote: We also want you to master SQL — not just SELECT statements, but complex joins, subqueries, window functions
performance optimization through indexing and query plans
Transaction management and ACID properties are covered extensively because real systems fail and you need to know what happens when they do.

We'll spend the last third of the semester on non-relational approaches. You'll work with document stores (MongoDB) and understand when NoSQL is the right choice versus when it's a hype-driven mistake.
CS3200.note: Planted depth gap: 'work with' MongoDB is hands-on, but only the written final covers NoSQL.

CS3200.quote: By the end you should also be comfortable with database administration basics — backup strategies, user permissions, and monitoring query performance in production.

CS4530.quote: Understand and apply common design patterns (Observer, Strategy, Factory, etc.)
Evaluate architectural tradeoffs between monolithic and microservice approaches
Practical experience decomposing requirements into software components
Work effectively in agile teams using Scrum practices (sprints, standups, retros)
Use Git workflows (branching, PRs, code review) in a team setting
Communicate technical decisions clearly in design documents and presentations
CS4530.note: Judgment call. IA1's written justification of each pattern and IA4's 'what to test and why' both make students explain technical decisions in writing. IA2 is a design document plus a presentation.

CS4530.quote: Develop comprehensive test strategies spanning unit, integration, and system tests
Apply test-driven development (TDD) as a design tool, not just verification
CS4530.note: IA4 is a strategy document, not TDD practice, and TP only asks for a test suite. Nothing assesses TDD.

CS4530.quote: Use static analysis and linting to maintain code quality
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions
Understand containerization basics (Docker) and why it matters for reproducibility
CS4530.note: Docker appears only in IA3's rubric keywords, not its description. The rubric is what's graded, so it counts.

CS4530.quote: Monitor application health and respond to production incidents

CS4550.quote: Build responsive user interfaces using React and modern CSS (Flexbox, Grid)
Design and implement RESTful APIs using Node.js and Express
Model data and write efficient queries using SQL and relational databases
CS4550.note: MP requires a PostgreSQL database, which counts even though it doesn't mention queries.

CS4550.quote: Apply authentication and authorization patterns (JWT, OAuth) to secure web apps
Write unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for both client and server code
CS4550.note: Intentional gap: no assignment asks students to write tests.

CS4550.quote: Deploy applications to cloud platforms and configure CI/CD pipelines

MIT6170.quote: Have improved your ability to analyze problems, explore and invent designs, present your work, and critique the work of others
MIT6170.note: Phase 4 critiques in P1-P3; pitch and peer reviews in FINAL

MIT6170.quote: Have developed a strong grasp of key software design notions (in particular, conceptual modeling, decoupling and abstraction) and improved skills in designing key components of a software system
MIT6170.note: All four require design documents or design phases

MIT6170.quote: Be able to build medium-scale web applications using standard technologies, conducting all phases of development from problem analysis to deployment
MIT6170.note: Only P1 mentions deployment, so the others cover it in part

MIT6170.quote: Have experienced the benefits and challenges of working in a team

MIT6005.quote: You will have the skills to develop a small to medium-scale software system from scratch: formulating and analyzing the problem to be solved; exploring and articulating candidate designs; implementing in Java; and using testing and reasoning to ensure quality.
MIT6005.note: The explorations count for implementing in Java only; P1-P3 require every part

MIT6005.quote: You will have a solid grasp of, and ability to apply, key software engineering ideas, including invariants, decoupling, and data abstraction.
MIT6005.note: Invariants in PS1-PS2, abstract types and coupling in P2, datatypes in P3; hints elsewhere not counted

MIT6005.quote: You will be fluent in three essential and widely used design notations (state machines, module dependency diagrams, and object models) and able to use them effectively in exploring and articulating problems and designs.
MIT6005.note: State machines in PS1, object models in PS3, diagrams required in all three projects

MIT6005.quote: You will be familiar with a variety of standard design and implementation patterns (such as model-view-controller and client-server) and with some popular technologies (such as Eclipse, JUnit, Subversion, Swing, HTTP, network sockets).
MIT6005.note: JUnit and patterns in the problem sets; Eclipse, HTTP, design patterns, Swing, MVC, sockets in the projects

MIT6005.quote: You will have a stronger inherent ability to make engineering judgments and pick the right tool for the task at hand; improved skills in design, organization and analysis; an appreciation for the importance of simplicity and abstraction; and a greater awareness of risk and how to mitigate it.
MIT6005.note: Design judgment in EX3, design decisions in PS2-PS3, compare designs and weigh risk in the projects

MIT6005.quote: You will have had some experience working collaboratively in a team.
MIT6005.note: Only the projects mention teammates, a team contract or team building
